author: p. f. gillen
title: Assemblyman Tri Ta discusses disaster aid tax policy and local support measures
text:
Assemblyman Tri Ta, who represents California’s 70th Assembly District, recently addressed several community issues and initiatives through a series of posts on his Twitter account.
On June 9, 2026, Tri Ta advocated for tax relief related to disaster compensation. He stated, “When families and businesses are forced to bear the costs of an evacuation, the state should not tax the compensation provided to make them whole. AB 760 ensures every dollar of compensation goes to families and businesses, not Sacramento.”
The following day, June 10, 2026, he recognized State Parks Week in California. In his post, he wrote, “Happy State Parks Week! California’s state parks give families the opportunity to experience the outdoors and connect with the places that make our state unique. Orange County is fortunate to be home to some of California’s most beautiful parks and beaches. Bolsa Chica State”
Later on June 10, Tri Ta highlighted support efforts for those affected by a recent chemical incident in Garden Grove. He posted, “Families and small businesses impacted by the Garden Grove chemical incident may be eligible for financial assistance through the Orange County United Way’s Community Resilience Fund. Eligible residents and businesses in Garden Grove, Stanton, Westminster, Cypress, Anaheim…”
Tri Ta’s comments come as part of ongoing legislative efforts in California addressing disaster response and community support programs.
